title: THE STAFF THAT SWALLOWED THE REST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did just as the Lord commanded. Aaron threw his staff down in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and it became a snake. Pharaoh then summoned wise men and sorcerers, and the Egyptian magicians also did the same things by their secret arts: Each one threw down his staff and it became a snake. But Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs." - Exodus 7:10-12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Aaron performs the sign, and Pharaoh's magicians immediately match it. Whatever their secret arts involved, the effect was enough to let Pharaoh dismiss the whole thing as a trick he had seen before.

Not everything impressive is from God. Scripture is realistic about counterfeit power and warns that even signs and wonders can deceive (2 Thess 2:9). We should not be naive, and we should never measure truth simply by how spectacular something looks.

But watch what happens next. Aaron's staff swallowed up their staffs. The imitation could go a certain distance, and then it was consumed.

That is the pattern. Counterfeits can copy, but they cannot conquer. They multiply displays; they do not deliver anyone. Pharaoh gained three more snakes and lost his staffs in the process.

Whatever imitations of God's power exist in this world, none of them can save. Only Christ has actually defeated death, and He did it in public.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I too easily impressed by spiritual displays without testing them?
2. What counterfeit source of power or comfort have I been leaning on?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me discernment to test what I see and hear. Keep me from being impressed by anything that cannot save. Amen.
